data.subject: Chemistry
data.question: (Error-analysis Numerical) While calculating mole fraction, a student ignores the moles of the solvent and considers only the moles of the solute. The calculated mole fraction will be:
solutions: Option A is correct because the denominator should include the total moles of solute and solvent.
Option B is incorrect because ignoring the solvent decreases the denominator and increases the calculated value.
Option C is incorrect because the calculation is incomplete.
Option D is incorrect because the mole fraction of a present solute cannot be zero.

data.subject: Chemistry
data.question: (HOTS) Which of the following changes will increase the concentration of dissolved CO₂ in a soft drink?
solutions: Option A is correct because high pressure and low temperature both increase the solubility of gases in liquids.
Option B is incorrect because both changes decrease gas solubility.
Option C is incorrect because increasing temperature decreases gas solubility.
Option D is incorrect because shaking an opened bottle accelerates the escape of CO₂.

data.subject: Chemistry
data.question: (Multi-step Numerical) A 0.20 molal aqueous solution of glucose is prepared. Calculate the boiling point of the solution. (Kb = 0.52 K kg mol⁻¹, boiling point of water = 100°C)
solutions: Option A is correct because ΔTb = 0.52 × 0.20 = 0.104°C, so boiling point = 100.104°C.
Option B is incorrect because it corresponds to a 1 molal solution.
Option C is incorrect because the calculation is incorrect.
Option D is incorrect because the boiling point elevation has been underestimated.

data.subject: Chemistry
data.question: (Multi-concept Numerical) Calculate the osmotic pressure of a 0.20 M glucose solution at 300 K. (R = 0.0821 L atm mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)
solutions: Option A is correct because π = CRT = 0.20 × 0.0821 × 300 = 4.93 atm.
Option B is incorrect because only half the concentration has effectively been considered.
Option C is incorrect because the calculation is incorrect.
Option D is incorrect because the value is doubled.

data.subject: Chemistry
data.question: (HOTS) A solution of acetic acid in benzene shows an experimental molar mass nearly twice the expected value. This is because acetic acid molecules undergo:
solutions: Option A is correct because acetic acid forms dimers in benzene through hydrogen bonding, increasing the apparent molar mass.
Option B is incorrect because dissociation decreases the apparent molar mass.
Option C is incorrect because hydrolysis does not occur in benzene.
Option D is incorrect because ionization in benzene is negligible.
